Number of studies.evidence_source: "This study contributes to the growing literature concerned with examining the associations between positive and negative body image and articulating what factors may either strengthen or attenuate this relationship (e.g., Swami & Tovee, 2009; Tiggemann & McCourt, 2013)."

section_summary.extract_value: The section describes a single study using an affect regulation framework to examine associations between body dissatisfaction and positive body image (body appreciation and body image flexibility), and how BMI relates to these constructs. It reports that BMI was a significant negative predictor of positive body image, that discrepancies between current and personal ideal body size were important, and highlights heavier Black older adolescent females showing higher dissatisfaction and lower positive body image. The section does not provide sample size, country, exact ages, assessment instruments, or correlation coefficients.
section_summary.evidence_source: "This study contributes to the growing literature..."; "Our regression findings largely mirrored the trend of bivariate associations delineating BMI as the most significant negative predictor of both forms of positive body image..."; "heavier Black older adolescent females reported higher body dissatisfaction and lower levels of both body appreciation and body image flexibility."
